title: Phase 6a: replace Postgres '~' regex in GetNextRootCardID (cards.go) — missed Phase 3 PG-ism
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Phase 3's PG-ism inventory checked ARRAY[ and = ANY($1) but NOT the Postgres regex match operator '~'. Two call sites survive:

- services/cards.go:810 — GetNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
- handlers/cards.go:494 — (s *Handler) getNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'

SQLite has no '~' regex operator (REGEXP requires a user-defined function). The query errors silently, returns empty, and GetNextRootCardID falls back to '1' instead of the correct MAX(numeric)+1. This breaks 3 handler tests (TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute, contributes to TestGetNextChildCardID) and is a REAL production bug post-cutover: every new root card would collide on id '1'.

Note these are duplicate implementations (services + handlers both inline the SQL). The handlers copy is the legacy dup; services.GetNextRootCardID is the canonical one (called from handlers/epub.go).

Fix: no cross-driver SQL expresses 'pure digits' (LIKE has no char classes on either DB; GLOB is SQLite-only). Pull the filter into Go: SELECT candidate card_id WHERE user_id/is_deleted, then filter with regexp.MustCompile('^[0-9]+$').MatchString and take the max via strconv.Atoi. At single-user scale this is trivial. Ideally dedupe the two impls onto the services one and have the handler call it.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Blocks the cards-id cluster of Zettelgarden-j89.
acceptance_criteria: GetNextRootCardID works identically on Postgres and SQLite; the '~' operator is gone from services/cards.go and handlers/cards.go; TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; no other PG regex operators remain in non-test Go (grep clean).
close_reason: Fixed in de7b122e. services.GetNextRootCardID now filters pure-numeric ids in Go (regexp) — no '~' operator remains in non-test Go (grep clean). Deduped the handler copy onto it. TestGetNextRootCardID + TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; full services/server/models/routes packages still green; handlers failures 11 -> 9.

title: Migrate Go backend from PostgreSQL to SQLite
description: Execute docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md. Goal: single static CGO-free Go binary + on-disk SQLite (WAL), no external DB process, zero behavior change, verified one-time import of ~15k cards. Phased: 0 pgvector swap, 1 spike, 2 schema, 3 query sweep, 4 cmd consolidation, 5 triggers->Go, 6 tests+ETL+cutover, 7a/7b cleanup.
notes: PHASE 6 COMPLETE 2026-07-28 — migration is cutover-ready. All phases 0-6 done: driver-neutral Go query code, triggers ported to Go, full test suite green on SQLite (no PG), ETL imports live dev DB (71 tables / 3,513,290 rows exact / 0 FK violations / idempotent), 560-comparison read-path A/B diff byte-identical PG vs SQLite, and the frontend renders identically on SQLite (gate 4 smoke). title: Phase 7a: SQLite cutover + Postgres removal from deploy/config
description:
Execute Phase 7a of docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md: the live cutover (Nick's call; involves app downtime) plus the code/config cleanup that flips SQLite to the default and removes Postgres from the deploy path.

This is the last blocking phase — Phases 0–6 are done (full suite green on SQLite; ETL verified against a copy of live zg_internal: 71 tables / 3,513,290 rows exact / 0 FK violations / idempotent; 560-comparison read-path A/B diff byte-identical; frontend smoke green).

## Part 1 — Cutover procedure (operational; ~30 min downtime)
Follow the Cutover Runbook in the design doc. Iterate against a COPY only; the final run is against the now-static live Postgres.
1. Stop the app (set read-only or halt the go_backend container).
2. Final insurance: `pg_dump -Fc zg_internal > zg_internal_dump-cutover-$(date +%Y%m%d).dump` — store off-host, keep ≥90 days. (Prior insurance dump from gate 1: /home/nick/zg_internal_dump-20260728-124426.dump, 111 MB.)
3. Build the ETL: `cd go-backend && go build -o migrate-pg-to-sqlite ./cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite`.
4. Run the final import against a fresh SQLite file: `./migrate-pg-to-sqlite --pg-dsn '<live DSN>' --sqlite-path ./data/zettelgarden.db`
5. Verification gates (do not proceed unless all green): per-table COUNT(*) PG==SQLite exact; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` clean; `PRAGMA integrity_check` ok; spot-check a few cards' body md5 + sub-graphs.
6. Flip config: `DB_DRIVER=sqlite`, `SQLITE_PATH=/app/data/zettelgarden.db`. Restart go_backend.
7. Smoke-test in prod: dashboard counts, a card detail, task list, chat history, create+edit a card.

## Part 2 — Code/config cleanup (lands with the flip)
- [ ] Remove the `db` (postgres:16-alpine) service from docker-zettel-run.yml + its `depends_on: service_healthy` on go_backend; mount the SQLite data dir instead.
- [ ] go-backend/.env.example: replace DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/NAME with `DB_DRIVER=sqlite` + `SQLITE_PATH=./data/zettelgarden.db`.
- [ ] server/database.go: `sql.Open("postgres", …)` ConnectToDatabase is already only called on the PG branch — confirm dead on the SQLite path; delete ResetDatabase (74c) or gate it on driver=="postgres".
- [ ] scripts/addParentId.go + scripts/computeKeywords.go: both are `//go:build ignore` one-shots; computeKeywords.go is already obsolete (references deleted llms.ComputeCardKeywords). Decide: archive both, or port to the driver abstraction. Recommend archive (they write none of the trigger-affected tables; re-run need is nil post-cutover).
- [ ] Update README.md self-hosting section (lines 62/89/97/100/125 — drop "PostgreSQL + pgvector"; "no external database"). Update AGENTS.md project note (line 4) "expects PostgreSQL" -> "SQLite (file), Typesense, AI keys".
- [ ] Document ongoing backup = `VACUUM INTO 'snapshot-$(date).db'` (NOT raw cp — unsafe under WAL without `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`).
- [ ] Optional fold-in: bn2 (RSS N+1) is independent and can land anytime.

## Notes
- lib/pq STAYS through the cutover window (Decision D6): models/notifications.go, handlers/schemas.go (pq.Error duplicate-key detection), server/database.go, and the ETL tool all still import it. Removal is Phase 7b, ~2 weeks after confirmed-prod.
- Keep Postgres running read-only ≥2 weeks post-cutover as fallback before 7b.
- Post-cutover day-2 backup: a one-time `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` then a `VACUUM INTO`, to establish the ongoing snapshot cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh clone -> DB_DRIVER=sqlite go run -> working app with no external database; cutover completed with all verification gates green; docker/env/README/AGENTS updated; Postgres removed from docker-zettel-run.yml; Postgres kept read-only as fallback.
notes: CUTOVER EXECUTED 2026-07-28 23:47-23:53 UTC — production (server-3 / 192.168.0.20, zg-internal) is now running on SQLite. Rehearsal ETL against live PG on .93 (read-only) passed; final ETL with app stopped: pg=3,514,707 sqlite=3,514,707 EXACT, 71 tables, 0 FK violations. Deep verify: integrity_check ok, fk_check empty, 14,544 cards/8,468 tasks/57,896 entities. Backend rebooted on SQLite ('Database connected and migrations completed successfully'); read+write paths confirmed live (scheduled_job_runs accumulating). Postgres on .93 untouched = read-only fallback (>=2 weeks); :pre-sqlite image retained on host for rollback; insurance pg_dump (116MB) on NAS. Originals backed up (.env.pre-sqlite, docker-compose.yml.pre-sqlite). NOTE: committed Dockerfile golang:1.22 -> golang:1.25 (go.mod requires go 1.25.0; the old pin broke the build). REMAINING under this issue = Part 2 repo cleanup only (README/AGENTS/.env.example, scripts decision, ResetDatabase/74c, VACUUM INTO docs). 7b stays ~2 weeks out.

title: Phase 6b: build pure-Go ETL tool to import Postgres -> SQLite (cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite)
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md Phase 6b. With Phase 6a done (full test suite green on SQLite, no Postgres), build the one-time ETL that imports the live ~15k-card Postgres DB into SQLite.

Scope (from the design doc Phase 6b):
- New cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite/ binary: reads live PG tables via lib/pq, writes SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, in FK-dependency order, preserving PKs verbatim so the graph (entity_card_junction, backlinks, task_dependencies, ...) stays intact.
- Pure-Go -- no CGO fallback. The Phase 1 bulk probe (spike/sqlite_bulk_timing_test.go) measured 15,000 card inserts in 780ms with one tx per insert; batched inserts will be faster.
- Idempotent / re-runnable: prefer INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pk) DO NOTHING over INSERT OR REPLACE (which fires DELETE+INSERT cascades). Alternative: disable FKs during bulk load, re-enable, then PRAGMA foreign_key_check. Run dozens of times during dev against a COPY of Postgres, never the live DB.
- Domain tables migrated verbatim (cards, card_tags, entities, entity_card_junction, facts, tasks, files, flashcards, summarizations, chat_*, notifications, user_*, rss_*, emails, audit_events, llm_jobs, llm_query_log, etc. -- full list in design doc). System tables (migrations, schema_definitions) rebuilt by the consolidated schema + migration runner, NOT migrated.
- Recommend wholesale migration of audit tables per design Open Question 2.

Highest-stakes remaining phase -- data continuity. Cutover Runbook protections apply (develop against a COPY; final pg_dump insurance; keep Postgres read-only >=2 weeks post-cutover).
acceptance_criteria: cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite/ builds (go build ./cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite) and successfully imports a COPY of the dev Postgres DB into a fresh SQLite file with: per-table row counts matching PG exactly; PRAGMA foreign_key_check clean; idempotent on re-run. Verification gates (Phase 6c) layered on top.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-07-28: Gate 1 GREEN. Ran end-to-end against a copy of live zg_internal (pg_dump -Fc -> zg_internal_copy; insurance dump /home/nick/zg_internal_dump-20260728-124426.dump, 111MB). 71 tables, 3,513,290 rows pg==sqlite EXACT. 0 FK violations. integrity_check ok. Idempotent (2nd run identical). 5-card byte-identical spot check (body md5 + structured_data + sub-graphs). Production binary boots on the migrated SQLite data. Two live-only fixes landed in commit f05a679d: (1) lib/pq returns _text arrays as []byte not string -> normalizeValue array branch now accepts both; (2) UUID-PK chat tables broke id MIN/MAX gate (PG has no MIN/MAX over uuid) -> hasIntegerPKID requires integer PK, regression test added. Schema drift flagged as Zettelgarden-0k6 (habits/habit_logs SQLite-only; 0144 dropped them from PG; non-blocking). Acceptance criteria fully met: builds, imports copy with exact counts, FK check clean, idempotent.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 6a: handler pool-vs-test-tx write isolation audit (s.DB vs s.GetDB())
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Dominant root cause behind the handlers test failures.

Mechanism: handlers.GetDB() returns the rolled-back per-test transaction (h.Server.Tx) in testing mode, but many handler methods write via the raw pool handle s.DB instead, which COMMITS for real. Reads that then go through GetDB() see a snapshot from before the write -> wrong result. Same mechanism leaks rows across tests (test pollution), since pool writes are never rolled back by Teardown.

Concrete confirmed case: handlers/auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute does s.DB.Exec('UPDATE users SET password = ...'). Then LoginRoute -> QueryUserByEmail (handlers/users.go:411) reads via s.GetDB() (the test tx, snapshot taken in Setup before the reset) -> sees the OLD password hash -> checkPasswordHash fails -> 401. TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess fails on SQLite; on Postgres MVCC the same staleness applies but the suite may have masked it by ordering. Other handlers using raw s.DB.Exec/Query (auth.go:352/383/413/449/475, plus JobRunner wired with S.DB in handlers/setup_test.go) are suspect.

Knock-on pollution (tests that pass in isolation but fail in the full suite because earlier pool-writes leak): TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags, and the 'database is locked' cleanup in TestGetNextChildCardID (pool write during an open tx).

Fix is a systematic audit, NOT a one-line change: route handler writes through GetDB() everywhere a test tx exists; reserve raw s.DB for the few places that genuinely need out-of-transaction access (and make them explicit). Source/JobRunner wiring (setup_test.go) should pass GetDB() too. Verify isolation holds by running the full handlers package (not just single tests).

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Largest lever among the remaining failures (~4-5 of the 11).
acceptance_criteria: No handler write path uses raw s.DB where a test-transaction-aware GetDB() is intended; TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess green on SQLite; cross-test card/prefs leakage (Typesense upsert of card 28, etc.) eliminated; documented convention for when raw pool access is legitimately required.
notes:
PART 1 LANDED 2026-07-27 (commit pending): routed two handler write paths through GetDB(): auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute (was s.DB.Exec UPDATE users password; the auth-reset test failed because the login read via s.GetDB()/tx couldn't see the pool-committed write) -- fixes TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess. entity.go: all 13 s.DB method-call sites -> s.GetDB() (the entity-card junction INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE writes were the prime pollution suspect for TestGetRelatedCards_Success; reads converted too for consistency). 2 sites kept as s.DB (GetEntities, NewDefaultClient) because their service signatures take *sql.DB, not the interface -- they are reads and don't pollute. Net: handlers failures 8 -> 7, no regressions.

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING (the rest of bto): converting handler WRITES alone is insufficient. The codebase has pervasive s.DB vs s.GetDB() handle INCONSISTENCY in TWO places that must be fixed TOGETHER:
1. TEST LAYER: cards_test.go has 15 sites calling services.CreateCard/UpdateCard(s.DB, ...) directly with the POOL (lines 617,630,742,754,766,778,790,839,851,906,925,938,950,963,994). CreateCard/UpdateCard do all the entity/backlink/fact writes, so pool calls COMMIT and leak across tests (test data is seeded once via sync.Once; pool writes accumulate). This is the source of TestGetRelatedCards_Success pollution (entity_card_junction deletions accumulate until card 1 has no shared entities) AND TestGetNextChildCardID nondeterminism.
2. HANDLER READ PATH: several reads use s.DB (pool), e.g. getNextChildCardID mixes handles within one function -- parent via s.GetDB() (tx) but children via services.GetChildCards(s.DB, ...) (pool). Converting ONLY the test layer breaks: a tx-local create becomes invisible to pool reads (regression observed: TestCheckChunkLinkedOrRelated_Integration broke when only tests were converted).

CORRECT FIX (part 2): convert BOTH together -- all remaining handler s.DB reads+writes to s.GetDB() (the ~80-site audit, minus legitimately-pool-only paths: Stripe webhooks in billing.go, OAuth callbacks in oauth.go, fire-and-forget last_login/last_seen) AND the 15 test-layer services.*(s.DB) calls. Verified directionally that this works but the full sweep needs care (scheduler/background paths where Server.Testing=true but no request tx exists are the risk). Recommend doing it file-by-file with the full suite as the gate.

NOT FIXED YET: TestGetRelatedCards_Success (pollution), TestGetNextChildCardID (handle-mix). The 2 stale status-code expectations (TestCreateCardLinkedParentId GET-expects-201, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags expects-200-route-returns-201) and 3 RSS network-dependent tests are SEPARATE pre-existing issues, not bto.
close_reason: Part 2 done (2026-07-27): service signatures widened to models.Database (LinkFactToCard, GetUserMemory/UpdateUserMemory, ReorderTaskStatuses refactored off its own Begin() onto handler-managed BeginTx); all handler request-scoped s.DB reads/writes -> s.GetDB(); 15 test-layer services.*(s.DB) calls -> tx; convention documented on Handler.GetDB(). handlers failures 7->0; full suite green on SQLite (no PG). Pre-existing non-SQLite test bugs also fixed (stale 201/200 expectations, getNextChildCardID majority-sep expectation, RSS tests de-networked via injectable services.FeedParser + strconv.Itoa URL fix). See status doc 'Phase 6a complete'.

title: Phase 6a: notification_preferences UPDATE is not an upsert (relies on a trigger that never existed)
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). handlers/notifications.go UpdatePreferences (line ~236) contains the comment 'This is handled by the trigger in the database' — but NO such trigger exists. Migration 0121 only runs a one-time INSERT INTO notification_preferences (user_id) SELECT id FROM users ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; there is no per-user auto-create trigger, and it was never ported to Go in Phase 5 (Phase 5 covered user_stats / llm_jobs / rss notifications, not this).

Consequence: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences does a plain UPDATE ... WHERE user_id = $1. When the user has no prefs row (common — e.g. test users inserted by importTestData, or any user created after the 0121 backfill), the UPDATE affects 0 rows, the handler's 'no rows' retry branch never fires (Exec returns no error), and the subsequent GetNotificationPreferences returns 'sql: no rows' -> handler returns 500 'Failed to get preferences'. This is a latent bug on BOTH Postgres and SQLite, not a SQLite regression.

Fix: make models.UpdateNotificationPreferences an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET ... (works identically on both drivers; the table PK is user_id). Drop the misleading trigger comment and the dead retry branch.

TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess is the failing test. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences is an upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE) or the handler creates-then-updates; works on both drivers; TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess green on SQLite; the misleading 'trigger' comment removed.
close_reason: Fixed in 1ccaefa8. models.UpdateNotificationPreferences is now INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE (cross-driver). Handler dead 'no rows' branch + misleading trigger comment removed. TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess green on SQLite; models+services packages green; handlers failures 9 -> 8.

title: Phase 6a follow-up: port handlers/facts.go + handlers/entity.go = ANY($1) + array_position to SQLite
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a (2026-07-26). Two production handler sites still use the Postgres array pattern that the services layer was fixed for in the same session:

- handlers/facts.go:808 -- WHERE f.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, f.id), called with pq.Array(factIDs)
- handlers/entity.go:1141 -- WHERE e.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, e.id), called with pq.Array(entityIDs)

The other 7 '= ANY($1)' sites were translated to IN (...) via the new models.InList / models.IntArgs helpers (models/sql.go). These 2 were deferred because they ALSO use 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' to preserve the input-slice order, which SQLite has no equivalent for.

Fix: translate '= ANY($1)' to 'IN ' || models.InList(1, len(ids)) (no fixed scalars here, so start at 1), drop the ORDER BY array_position clause, bind via models.IntArgs(ids)..., then reorder the scanned rows app-side to match the input ids order (collect into a map[id]row, emit in input order). Drop the lib/pq import from both files. Verify on both drivers.

These currently fail at runtime on SQLite with 'no such function: ANY' / 'no such function: array_position', contributing to TestGetRelatedCards_Success and the fact-link handler failures. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: handlers/facts.go and handlers/entity.go run unchanged on Postgres and SQLite; pq.Array removed from both; the similar-facts / similar-entities result order matches the input ids; lib/pq import dropped from both files; relevant handler tests green on SQLite.
close_reason: Fixed in 07940bd6. handlers/{facts,entity}.go GetSimilar* now use 'IN '+models.InList(1,len(ids)) bound via models.IntArgs(ids)..., with app-side reorder (map-by-id -> emit in ranked input order) replacing ORDER BY array_position. lib/pq dropped from both files. Zero = ANY/array_position/pq.Array remain in non-test Go (grep clean). New idiom smoke test TestSimilarityInListAndAppSideReorder green; all non-handlers packages green; handlers still 8 (these handlers have no direct unit test -- need a Typesense stub).

title: Phase 6a: run full Go test suite green against SQLite (rewrite tests/conftest.go PG-isms)
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md Phase 6a. Goal: `go test ./...` green with NO Postgres running -- the test suite defaults to an in-memory SQLite DB built from the consolidated schema.

Scope of conftest.go changes (verified by reading the file):
1. setTestEnvironmentVariables: default DB_DRIVER=sqlite + SQLITE_PATH=:memory: (override with DB_DRIVER=postgres to keep the PG path). Mirror bootstrap.InitServer's driver selection.
2. Setup(): branch on cfg.Database.Driver -- OpenSQLite(:memory:) vs ConnectToDatabase; SchemaDir=.../schema/sqlite for sqlite (so RunMigrations loads schema.sqlite.sql via the Phase 1 splitter); set S.Driver; SKIP the PG-only ResetDatabase on sqlite (it CASCADE/SERIAL -- the :memory: DB is fresh each run).
3. importTestData: the line `SELECT setval('entities_id_seq', ...)` (line ~503) is PG-only -- guard on driver. On SQLite, explicit-id inserts into entities auto-advance AUTOINCREMENT/max-rowid, so no manual reset is needed (no collision).
4. truncateTestData() is DEAD CODE (grep confirms zero callers) -- tx-per-test rollback (Teardown) handles all isolation. Leave as-is; out of scope.

The long tail: Phase 3 swept NON-TEST Go only, so individual *_test.go files across handlers/ and services/ still contain PG-isms (TRUNCATE, setval, ARRAY, ::, etc.) that will surface once the suite runs on SQLite. Iterate to green.

Lean on the existing tx-per-test rollback -- rolled-back transactions never commit, so there is nothing to reset per test.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j. Builds on the closed Phase 1/2/3/5 work.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./...` exits green from a clean checkout with no Postgres process running (DB_DRIVER unset -> sqlite default). The existing PG test path still works if DB_DRIVER=postgres is set.
notes:
IN PROGRESS 2026-07-26: 12/14 Go packages green vs SQLite (no PG). Only handlers remains: 11 failing tests (down from a 600s deadlock). Committed as b2532498.

Remaining 11 handlers failures (clusters):
- Card-ID generation (3): TestGetNextRootCardID{,Route}, TestGetNextChildCardID -- 'expected ID 11, got 1'; MAX(id)+1 / sequence semantics under test-data reduction.
- TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags (3) -- card/fact/relation paths.
- RSS (3): Test{Star,Unstar,ListStarred}RSSArticleRoute -- 'Failed to create test feed: status 400'.
- TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess (1) -- login 401 after reset (pool write vs test tx visibility).
- TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess (1) -- 'Failed to get preferences'.

Known production-code PG-isms still unfixed (tracked in Zettelgarden-j8q): handlers/facts.go:808 + handlers/entity.go:1141 still use '= ANY($1)' + 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' + pq.Array -- need IN(...) expansion via models.InList/IntArgs + app-side reorder. See status doc 'Phase 6a progress'.
close_reason: Phase 6a complete (2026-07-27): go test ./... green against SQLite with NO Postgres running (DB_DRIVER unset -> sqlite default). All 14 Go packages pass. tests/conftest.go branches on driver (temp file-backed SQLite so WAL engages), skips PG-only ResetDatabase, guards the one setval. Acceptance criterion met. title: SQLite boot wiring: create SQLITE_PATH parent dir + RunMigrations integration test
description:
Two leftover items flagged in the Phase 2 hotfix (docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-status.md), to be done before the first real DB_DRIVER=sqlite run:

1. OpenSQLite (server/sqlite.go) does not yet create the SQLITE_PATH parent directory. Default SQLITE_PATH is ./data/zettelgarden.db, which requires ./data/ to exist -- otherwise first boot fails. MkdirAll the parent dir before opening.

2. No test exercises the real RunMigrations against ./schema/sqlite. Add an integration test that boots an in-memory (or temp file) SQLite, runs RunMigrations pointed at the consolidated schema dir, and asserts the schema loaded (e.g. a known table exists, foreign_key_check passes).

This unblocks Phase 5 work and the first real DB_DRIVER=sqlite boot.
notes:
Done. (1) OpenSQLite now MkdirAlls the SQLITE_PATH parent dir (TestOpenSQLiteCreatesParentDir). (2) Added TestRunMigrationsAppliesConsolidatedSchema exercising real ./schema/sqlite end-to-end (core tables, exactly 1 migration recorded, foreign_key_check clean).

LATENT BOOT BUG FOUND + FIXED: the integration test surfaced that the consolidated schema declared a 'migrations' table identical to the one RunMigrations bootstraps -> first DB_DRIVER=sqlite boot would fatal 'table migrations already exists'. title: Phase 2 follow-up: drop habits/habit_logs from consolidated SQLite schema (mirror migration 0144)
description:
Surfaced by the first live ETL run (Phase 6c gate 1, 2026-07-28). The live dev Postgres DB no longer has habits/habit_logs: migration 0144-remove-habits-feature.sql dropped them (0131/0132 added them). But the consolidated SQLite schema (schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql, generated from the 2026-07-25 pg_dump snapshot which predated 0144 being applied to that snapshot) still contains both tables, so they show up as 'SQLite-only skipped' (2 tables) in the ETL's PG∩SQLite intersection.

Impact is nil: no Go code references habits (grep finds nothing), the ETL correctly skips them (no PG data -> no data loss), and they'd just be empty tables after cutover. But it is real schema drift: the consolidated schema is out of sync with production.

Fix: mirror 0144 in the SQLite world -- either remove the habits/habit_logs CREATE TABLE (+ any indexes) from schema.sqlite.sql, or append a SQLite-side drop migration, so a fresh SQLite install matches the post-0144 PG schema. Verify by re-running the ETL and confirming the 'SQLite-only skipped' set is empty.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j. Not a blocker for cutover (Phase 7a cleanup is also acceptable).
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated SQLite schema no longer contains habits or habit_logs; ETL run reports 0 SQLite-only-skipped tables; go test ./... still green.
close_reason: Closed 2026-07-28: removed habits + habit_logs CREATE TABLEs and their 6 indexes from schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql (mirrors PG migration 0144-remove-habits-feature.sql). No Go code references habits (grep clean); the only FK was habit_logs->habits (internal). Table count 72 -> 71; TestConsolidatedSchemaLoads green (FK + integrity check ok); full go test ./... green; go build ok. A fresh SQLite install now matches post-0144 production; the ETL's SQLite-only-skipped set will be empty on the next run.

title: Phase 5 follow-up: collapse N+1 in syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate (services/rss_notifications.go)
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/rss_notifications.go syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate() (used by MarkRSSFeedAsRead and MarkRSSFolderAsRead in services/rss.go) issues one GetRSSArticleByID SELECT per matched article -- an N+1. The original PG trigger had the full row in hand and fired once per row, so this is a small perf regression. Acceptable at single-user scale, but a large feed/folder mark-read would feel it.

Fix is small: change the helper to SELECT the full rss_articles columns (not just id) in its single predicate query, hydrate models.RSSArticle directly, and call SyncRSSArticleNotification without the per-row GetRSSArticleByID round-trip. Keep it best-effort (log + continue).

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: MarkRSSFeedAsRead / MarkRSSFolderAsRead issue exactly 1 SELECT for the article set (no per-row GetRSSArticleByID); notification sync behaviour unchanged; existing rss_notifications_sqlite_test.go still green.

title: Phase 7a: drop or modernize PG-only ResetDatabase in server/database.go
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 1-5 SQLite review (2026-07-26). server/database.go ResetDatabase() is still fully PG-specific: CASCADE on every DROP TABLE, SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, DROP TABLE ... CASCADE, etc. It is NOT on the SQLite code path (SQLite uses bootstrap + RunMigrations), so it is harmless today, but it is a latent inconsistency that will confuse readers post-cutover.

Action: as part of Phase 7a (cleanup & rollout), either (a) delete ResetDatabase entirely if nothing calls it on the SQLite path, or (b) gate it on S.Driver == 'postgres' and add a SQLite equivalent (or a no-op). While there, confirm no callers remain that assume PG semantics.

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: ResetDatabase either removed or driver-gated; no PG-only SQL remains on the SQLite boot path; backend still boots on both drivers.

title: file_count in user_stats never decrements (files only soft-deleted)
description:
Pre-existing bug surfaced during SQLite Phase 5 scoping (2026-07-25). The user_stats.file_count counter only ever INCREMENTS: the old PG trigger trg_files_delete fired AFTER DELETE (hard delete), but the Go server only ever soft-deletes files (UPDATE files SET is_deleted=true in handlers/files.go DeleteFileRoute). So file_count grows monotonically and overcounts over time.

Decision (Nick, 2026-07-25): leave current behavior as-is for now; do NOT fix as part of Phase 5. Track here. When fixing, decrement file_count in the Go files soft-delete path (and consider whether hard-deletes should ever happen).

title: Phase 5 follow-up: harden userstats addAmount $2-twice param reuse against driver version bumps
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/userstats.go addAmount() references $2 twice in one statement (once in VALUES, once in the ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET) and binds a single positional arg. modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0 and lib/pq both correctly bind the same arg to both occurrences (verified by services/userstats_sqlite_test.go which accumulates to ~0.20 llm_cost / 750 revenue), so this works today on both drivers.

The concern is purely future-proofing: reuse of a numbered param is the one construct in the SQLite migration that is most sensitive to a modernc version bump changing how repeated numbered params are bound.

Options if it ever breaks (low priority): (a) bind the amount twice from the caller side ($2 and $3), or (b) switch to a named param via sql.Named. No action needed today -- this issue exists purely as a breadcrumb so a future 'user_stats add failed' after a go.mod bump is diagnosable in seconds.

Not a blocker for anything. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: If a modernc bump ever breaks repeated numbered-param binding, addAmount is updated (bind twice or use sql.Named) and services/userstats_sqlite_test.go confirms both llm_cost and revenue accumulate correctly.

value: Postgres->SQLite migration (epic Zettelgarden-c7j) reached cutover-ready 2026-07-28: all of Phase 6 green. Cutover procedure = the Cutover Runbook in docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md (stop app -> final pg_dump insurance -> run cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite against static PG -> run 6c gates -> flip DB_DRIVER=sqlite+SQLITE_PATH -> restart -> smoke -> keep PG read-only >=2 weeks). ETL is dynamic PG∩SQLite intersection copy with foreign_keys=OFF load + PRAGMA foreign_key_check. Insurance dump from 2026-07-28 at /home/nick/zg_internal_dump-20260728-124426.dump (dev host). SQLite migration Phase 5 LIVE write paths to port (verified 2026-07-25). user_stats (0093) is ONLY trigger-maintained today (zero Go writes). Port counters at: cards INSERT services/cards.go:869 + soft-delete :655 (DeleteCard); tasks INSERT services/tasks.go:500 + soft-delete :531 (DeleteTask); files INSERT handlers/files.go:596; llm_query_log INSERT services/llms.go:132 (+=cost_usd); revenue INSERT handlers/billing.go:248 (+=amount_cents). rss notifications (0124 + rss part of 0122): rss_articles INSERT services/rss.go:639; star/unstar handlers/handlers.go:658/681; read services/rss.go:407/425/443; UPDATE :516; DELETE services/jobs/rss_article_cleanup_job.go:77 -- reuse models.CreateNotification + CalculateImportanceScore + GetFilterTagsForRSS. llm_jobs updated_at (0096): 3 of 4 UPDATE sites already set updated_at (models/job.go:326/339/350); only services/jobrunner.go:123 CleanupStale needs it added.

SQLite migration Phase 5 scoping: several 'triggers to port' are actually DEAD in the Go server because there is no Go write path. Verified 2026-07-25: (1) chat_messages + chat_conversations have NO Go INSERT/writer (no chat routes/handlers; only read in stats + dropped in reset) -> triggers 0067 (conversation timestamp) and the chat_message_count part of 0093 need no port. (2) emails table has NO Go ingestion (no email routes/handlers; only incidental refs) -> email-notification trigger 0123 + email part of 0122 helper need no port. (3) llm_jobs pg_notify trigger 0102 is DEAD: no LISTEN anywhere in Go (grep hits are net.Listen/signal.Notify). (4) files are only ever SOFT-deleted in Go (is_deleted=true), so the AFTER DELETE file_count trigger (trg_files_delete in 0093) never fires -> file_count only increments today (pre-existing bug).
